gaps.obligationText: A firm must send the customer a final response within 15 business days of receiving a complaint.
gaps.description: Policy POL-CMP-01 requires a final response within 30 calendar days whereas the obligation mandates 15 business days, which is a longer deadline that does not meet the requirement.

gaps.obligationText: A firm must retain records of each complaint, including all correspondence with the customer, for at least 7 years from the final response.
gaps.description: Policy A retains complaint files for 7 years after the final response (matching the obligation), but Policy B deletes customer communications including complaint correspondence after only 5 years from creation, which would violate the 7-year retention requirement for complaints.

gaps.noticeTitle: Third-party AI models in credit decisions
gaps.obligationText: The model risk committee must review each third-party AI model in the inventory at least once a year, including its performance and fairness results.
gaps.description: The obligation requires review of "each third-party AI model in the inventory" at least annually, but POL-MRM-01 only covers models "built by the bank" and POL-TPR-01 reviews "suppliers that support important business services" without specifically covering third-party AI models or their performance and fairness results.

gaps.noticeTitle: Third-party AI models in credit decisions
gaps.obligationText: A firm must maintain an inventory of third-party AI models used in consumer credit decisions, recording the supplier, purpose and the products affected.
gaps.description: The obligation requires maintaining an inventory specifically of third-party AI models with supplier, purpose and affected products, but POL-TPR-01 only maintains a general supplier register with criticality ratings and POL-MRM-01 addresses only internally built models, neither capturing the required inventory of third-party AI models used in consumer credit decisions.
